title: Implementer brief: re-anchor the spec first and self-check before reporting

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Retrospective R2 and R4 (docs/review-2026-10-25-relay-retrospective.md). Line anchors drift as slices land, and every orchestrator re-anchored by hand. 23 of 28 relays needed a fix round; the Review FAIL notes cluster in races and handle lifetime, docs out of step with code, and tests that pass when wiring is removed. Role prompts are ork's own text (roles.prompts).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md`: add a first step (re-anchor Files and Failing tests from the current code; report changes under a Spec edits line) and a self-check list before the report.
- `internal/roles/roles.go`: only if the prompt is assembled there.
- Tests: `internal/roles/roles_test.go` (prompt text order).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestImplementerPromptReanchorsFirst: the re-anchor step comes before the implement step.
- TestImplementerPromptSelfCheck: the self-check names concurrency and handle lifetime, docs updated with code, and a test that fails when the wiring is removed, before the report section.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Edit the embedded implementer prompt only. Keep it free of Claude Code-only mechanics. Do not change the report shape (role.report-shape). Track the fix-round rate on the next waves to see whether it helps; do not claim it does.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: go test -race ./internal/roles ./internal/engine; go vet; gofmt -l; slicer check; adj lint.
